claims.claim: SIR has one-way S→I→R transition while SIS permits reinfection after recovery; transition rules, not graph topology alone, determine dynamics.
claims.locator: Newman 2002, SIR model description; compare SIS discussion in Pastor-Satorras 2001

claims.claim: For m conditionally independent infectious contacts of equal per-contact probability beta, infection chance is 1-(1-beta)^m.
claims.locator: Derived from independent edge-transmission probability under the specified model

claims.claim: For locally tree-like uncorrelated configuration networks, the epidemic/giant-outbreak threshold in an SIR bond-percolation approximation uses transmissibility T and excess-degree branching factor.
claims.locator: Newman 2002, network percolation and degree generating functions

claims.claim: SIS heterogeneous mean-field threshold lambda_c=<k>/<k^2> is distinct from SIR bond-percolation threshold and is approximation-dependent.
claims.locator: Pastor-Satorras and Vespignani 2001, degree-resolved SIS mean-field analysis

claims.claim: Finite network degree cutoffs and correlations affect observed epidemic thresholds.
claims.locator: Pastor-Satorras and Vespignani 2002, finite size scaling

claims.claim: On a five-node path, synchronous one-step SIR with p=1 infects one new vertex per step and has infected counts [1,1,1,1,1,0].
claims.locator: Derived from explicitly specified update function and path_graph(5)
